mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Taiwanese Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: notarize with a Taiwan notary, then verify through the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) after submission to the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office. Hague Apostille is not applicable and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Registration of Representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only via SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification. Hague Apostille does not apply and must not be sequenced with this path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Authorizing WFOE Formation and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwanese Shareholder, notarized by a Taiwan District Court-certified notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: notarization followed by SEF/ARATS verification. Apostille is mutually exclusive and must not be added.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Company Charter) of Taiwanese Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (filed copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: certified copy issued by Taiwan company registry, notarized, then processed through SEF/ARATS verification. No apostille chain permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from Taiwanese Corporate Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Taiwan bank supervised by the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: bank officer signature notarized, then SEF/ARATS verification. This is a standalone legalization path; Apostille cannot be applied.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration and UBO Register Extract of Taiwanese Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Company Registry / Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission-filed UBO register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only through SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification; Hague Apostille is inapplicable and must not be chained sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all shareholders, UBOs, directors, senior managers, and power-of-attorney holders against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, PRC government-designated terrorism and sanctions lists, and Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission AML blacklists. PEP status must be identified for individuals holding prominent public functions in any country, including Taiwan and mainland China, as well as family members and close associates. Any positive hit requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds documentation, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Screenings must be repeated at onboarding, at each material transaction, and at least quarterly, with records retained for at least five years after termination of the relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and SAMR Enterprise Registration Online Name Reservation Module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in simplified Chinese characters. A Chinese trade name is mandatory; pinyin or English names may be supplementary but cannot replace the statutory Chinese name. The four-tier naming convention applies: (1) administrative division; (2) distinctive trade name of at least two Chinese characters; (3) industry or scope description aligning with ISIC 6201; and (4) organizational form 'Limited Liability Company'. Phonetic transliteration must follow standard Putonghua pronunciation and avoid identical or highly similar rendering to prohibited or sensitive tokens.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain the written SAMR rejection notice from the online portal within 15 days. A reconsideration application must be filed with the original SAMR bureau or the next higher SAMR bureau, attaching the rejection notice, a detailed explanation of business relevance, and any ministerial approval documents. The appellate authority must issue a written decision within 30 days. If the name remains denied, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration before the local People's Government or SAMR, followed by administrative litigation in the competent People's Court. A pending appeal allows the name reservation window to be extended for an additional 30-day period upon written motion.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a WFOE engaged in cloud vulnerability scanning and penetration testing SaaS, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable. SAMR, the local tax authority, and the bank require a physical presence at a registered address where employees, servers or remote IT infrastructure, and corporate records can be inspected. The Cyberspace Administration of China's data-security and licensing regimes further demand physical office substance. A mailbox-only address will cause rejection of tax registration, bank account opening, and may trigger administrative penalties or revocation of the business license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 75% within the first 12 months. Inspection checklist: (1) original lease agreement matching the registered address; (2) visible company signage; (3) on-site presence of the legal representative or authorized manager; (4) maintenance of statutory books, seals, and IT hardware logs; (5) employee attendance and social-insurance records; (6) network-security compliance documentation for the SaaS platform. Municipal tax and SAMR authorities conduct unannounced checks under the 'Doubly Random, Publicly Released' supervision model.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (as amended), Articles 1-10, 128-156, 172-174, 192-193, 208-210, 218-220, 387-388; Investment Approval under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 1-10.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (Form 1) together with the Articles of Incorporation and Foreign Investment Approval Certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Taiwan law does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for limited liability companies. However, the subscribed capital must be fully paid in cash or in-kind as stated in the Articles, and the capital must be deposited in a bank account in the company's name prior to registration. No escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company'), a wholly foreign-owned enterprise incorporated under the laws of Taiwan, held on [DATE] at [TIME] at the registered office of the Company, [ADDRESS]. PRESENT: All directors of the Company, being [DIRECTOR NAMES], constituting a quorum. The Chairman of the meeting, [CHAIRMAN NAME], called the meeting to order and stated that the purpose of the meeting is to adopt certain resolutions necessary for the initial organization and operation of the Company. After due deliberation, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED, that the Company's authorized share capital is [AMOUNT] New Taiwan Dollars (NTD) divided into [NUMBER] shares of NTD [PAR VALUE] each, and that the initial subscribed and paid-up capital is [AMOUNT] NTD, fully subscribed by the sole shareholder, [SHAREHOLDER NAME], a foreign entity. The Board acknowledges receipt of the capital contribution and directs the officers to file the capital verification report with the competent authority. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Company shall open a corporate bank account with [BANK NAME] at [BRANCH], and that the Chairman, the President, and the Chief Financial Officer, or any two of them acting jointly, are hereby authorized to execute all banking documents, sign checks, and manage the Company's funds in accordance with the Company's internal control policies. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [FULL ADDRESS], Taiwan, and that the Company shall file the necessary notices with the Department of Commerce and the local tax authority. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed to the offices indicated: [NAME] as Chairman of the Board, [NAME] as President, [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME] as Corporate Secretary. Each officer shall serve until the next annual general meeting or until a successor is duly elected. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to execute all documents, pay all fees, and take all actions necessary to complete the incorporation and registration of the Company, including but not limited to filing the Articles of Incorporation, obtaining the Foreign Investment Approval, and registering for tax identification numbers. The meeting was adjourned. Dated this [DATE]. Certified by: [SECRETARY NAME], Corporate Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) and Department of Commerce, MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor must first submit an application for foreign investment approval to the Investment Commission, MOEA, providing the proposed company name, business scope, capital amount, and shareholder details. Upon approval, the investor shall reserve the company name with the Department of Commerce via the online Company Name Reservation System. The name must not conflict with existing registered names and must comply with the Company Act naming rules. The reservation is valid for six months and may be renewed. The application must be notarized if submitted from abroad, and all documents must be in Chinese or accompanied by certified translations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor (notarized and apostilled)
Power of Attorney for local agent (if any)
Proof of identity of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected, the applicant may file an appeal with the Department of Commerce within 30 days, providing alternative names. If the foreign investment application is queried, the applicant shall submit additional documentation within 15 days; failure to respond may result in rejection, but a new application can be filed after rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (or local court notary) and the Department of Commerce, MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Articles of Incorporation must be drafted in Chinese, containing the company name, business scope, capital structure, share classes, director and supervisor provisions, and registered office address. The document must be signed by all initial shareholders and directors. If any shareholder is a foreign entity, the signature must be notarized in the home country and then legalized by the Taiwan representative office or apostilled. The notarized Articles shall be submitted to the Department of Commerce as part of the registration package. The Articles must comply with the mandatory provisions of the Company Act, including the number of directors (at least one) and the establishment of a supervisor if required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the Department of Commerce identifies defects in the Articles, the applicant shall amend and re-notarize the document. The Department may issue a notice of correction with a 14-day deadline; failure to correct results in rejection, but a fresh application can be filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration with the Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The applicant shall file the complete registration package, including the notarized Articles, the Foreign Investment Approval Certificate, the capital deposit certificate, and the name reservation certificate, via the MOEA's online registration system or in person. The Department will review the documents for legal compliance, including the adequacy of the capital, the legality of the business scope, and the appointment of officers. Upon approval, the Department issues a Company Registration Certificate. The company must also register for tax identification (Uniform Invoice Number) with the National Taxation Bureau within 15 days of registration.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of directors and shareholders
Power of Attorney for the local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is suspended, the applicant shall respond to the Department's query within 20 days. If the suspension is due to missing documents, the applicant may submit them within the same period. If the registration is rejected, the applicant may appeal to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days, or re-file after correcting the deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Compliance and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Administration, local labor authority, and the chosen commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Registration Certificate, the company shall: (a) obtain a tax identification number (TIN) and register for business tax; (b) open a corporate bank account with the chosen bank, presenting the registration certificate and the board resolution authorizing signatories; (c) register as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration; (d) file the initial capital verification report with the Department of Commerce if required; and (e) obtain any industry-specific permits if applicable (not applicable for pure digital SaaS). The company must also appoint a statutory auditor if required by the Company Act based on capital thresholds.
required_dossiers: Labor insurance and health insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is delayed, the company may be subject to penalties; the company should apply for an extension if necessary. If the bank account opening is delayed due to compliance checks, the company shall provide additional due diligence documents as requested by the bank. Any adverse action can be cured by submitting the required documents and paying any late fees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, via the National Electronic Tax Bureau portal (e-Tax platform) at etax.chinatax.gov.cn; local tax service branches administer entity-level registration and compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation, the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) obtains a business license carrying the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). The SAMR data is automatically shared with the State Taxation Administration, and the WFOE must complete tax registration within 30 days by accessing the National Electronic Tax Bureau, submitting the business license, legal representative identification, articles of association, registered address proof, bank account information, and the completed tax registration declaration. The tax authority issues the tax registration certificate and the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), which is the 18-digit USCC. For a non-resident enterprise such as the Taiwanese parent company that has no establishment in China, a non-resident TIN is obtained separately by filing the non-resident enterprise tax registration form, either directly with the competent tax authority or through the local withholding agent appointed by the WFOE.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for basic tax registration; every Chinese entity must register within 30 days of business license issuance. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies when annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000 for modern services, including SaaS; voluntary registration is permitted below that threshold. Small-scale taxpayers with monthly sales below CNY 100,000 may use the simplified exemption regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the fully digitalized electronic invoice (shu-dian-piao) system through the State Taxation Administration's Unified Electronic Invoice Service Platform. VAT invoices must be issued via tax-authority-approved software or the official electronic invoice platform, which performs automatic real-time transmission, taxation control, anti-forgery digital stamping, invoice verification, and risk analysis. There is no public third-party API; certified invoicing systems must integrate with the tax authority's official electronic tax clearance interfaces.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Cross-border supply of information technology services, including cloud vulnerability scanning and penetration testing SaaS, qualifies for 0% VAT under the State Taxation Administration's Catalogue of Cross-Border Taxable Services Eligible for Zero Rating or Exemption, provided the recipient is an offshore entity or individual, the service is wholly consumed outside China, no Chinese non-resident entity derives a benefit from the service within China, and the taxpayer maintains contractual, invoicing, payment, and delivery evidence proving the offshore place of use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) - applicable to any physical media, appliance, or hardware delivered from China
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill - for physical goods exports
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) / International Revenue Declaration Form evidencing cross-border receipt
Executed service contract with the offshore recipient and a place-of-consumption statement
Zero-rated VAT invoice issued through the electronic invoicing platform
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities may perform post-export verification and require the full documentation bundle above. If zero-rating is not substantiated, the output VAT becomes payable at the applicable domestic service rate, with late payment surcharge (0.05% per day) and administrative penalties for tax evasion under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection, ranging from 50% to 500% of the deficient tax amount. Fraudulent export zero-rating or invoicing carries civil monetary penalties, retrospective clawback of refunded input VAT, and criminal liability under the Criminal Law for export tax fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, delegated by the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China operates a managed floating RMB exchange-rate regime with current-account convertibility and strict capital-account supervision. A WFOE may legitimately convert RMB for genuine trade, service, and salary-related operational payments, but conversion of foreign equity capital, shareholder loans, divestment proceeds, and repatriated profits remains subject to SAFE scrutiny. Each conversion must be executed by a designated foreign-exchange bank with truthful documentation, including the underlying contract, invoices, tax receipts, and, for capital items, the FDI foreign-exchange registration. Surplus RMB generated from converted capital cannot be freely re-converted into foreign currency; outbound remittances are limited to audited distributable profits, approved reductions, or liquidation proceeds. For a cybersecurity SaaS exporter, current-account receipts must correspond to actual service contracts and cannot be used to justify disguised capital flows. Dividend remittances require annual statutory audit, tax clearance, board resolution, and bank-level verification that the profit has legal retained-earnings basis. Therefore, treasury officers should treat onshore RMB as operationally convertible only under genuine underlying transactions and maintain clear segregation between FDI capital, operational cash, and taxed profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export-proceeds surrender ratio applies in mainland China; the mandatory conversion ratio is zero and the WFOE may retain 100% of export receipts in its foreign-exchange settlement account. Export proceeds must still be repatriated to a mainland bank account, unless SAFE-approved offshore retention is obtained, and goods-export receivables are generally expected within 90 days from the customs export declaration date under the total-amount verification system; longer collection terms require enterprise-level registration with the bank/SAFE. Any conversion from foreign currency to RMB is made at the WFOE's election and must be supported by genuine underlying trade or service documents. For cybersecurity SaaS/service exports, the collection timing follows the contract and invoice maturity, with the bank verifying service delivery before allowing settlement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account (Capital Escrow Account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account plus Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
FDI Capital Settlement Account (Capital Escrow Account)
General Operating Account and Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low. Offshore digital EMI providers (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Currenxie) are not licensed by PBOC/SAFE to open a WFOE's FDI capital account, to receive equity capital contributions, or to complete SAFE foreign-exchange registration and capital verification. They cannot convert FDI capital into RMB or issue the statutory inward post-registration notices. The WFOE must maintain primary clearing with a domestic Tier-1 bank. EMIs may only be used as ancillary technical rails for outbound operating payments if they have an onshore partner-bank settlement route and the underlying service is recorded as a current-account transaction; even then, all funds flow into and out of the domestic bank account, so the EMI does not act as an independent bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative or a duly authorized senior officer (with notarized power of attorney) must appear physically at the onshore bank branch for the FDI capital account opening interview. Remote video KYC is generally insufficient for the initial capital account and for the first disbursement-request confirmation. Some Tier-1 banks will permit the legal representative to sign remotely only after an in-person onboarding of the financial controller and the corporate seal has been physically deposited, but consular proxy opening is not recognized as a substitute for physical appearance. All corporate chops, original establishment documents, and investor board resolutions must be presented for on-site inspection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-ownership matrix where the Taiwan parent holds the WFOE through an intermediate Hong Kong/BVI vehicle, obscuring the ultimate individual shareholders and creating a horizontal UBO red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ownership chart to ultimate natural persons; certified copies of Taiwan company registration, Hong Kong/BVI registry extracts, and articles of association; notarized beneficial-ownership declarations from every intermediate entity; passport and proof-of-address documents for all UBOs; parent board resolution approving the capital contribution; source-of-wealth statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Oversized or back-loaded capital injection inconsistent with the stated registered capital plan, raising suspicion of money laundering through equity masking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call schedule in the amended articles and investment approval; bank statements showing the parent's retained earnings; audited financial statements of the parent for the funded years; tax return filings of the Taiwan parent; share-transfer and capital contribution agreement; bank capital-contribution confirmation after each wired tranche; CPA capital verification report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cybersecurity SaaS activities are classified as sensitive data processing and may trigger the bank's enhanced KYC review due to possible cross-border data transfer, export control, and national-security exposure under PRC Cybersecurity Law and Data Security Law.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business license limited to lawful cybersecurity services; ICP/network-security filing if applicable; ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II certificates; MLPS (Multi-Level Protection Scheme) grading and security testing report; contracts showing penetration testing is confined to customer-authorized systems; data-flow map and cross-border transfer impact assessment; written undertaking on no unlawful data export; export-classification statement confirming the SaaS does not fall within controlled technology export categories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High daily volumes of low-value subscription receipts from overseas SaaS clients create mismatches between aggregate settlement batches and individual invoices, triggering false-trade and trade-round-tripping screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment gateway agreements with settlement schedule; subscriber agreements and usage logs; monthly aggregated payout statements; matching invoice register and VAT zero-rated or export-tax-favored proof; bank treasury rule allowing application of aggregated receipts to recurring subscriptions; independent auditor's ISAE 3402 report on the billing system; process flow documenting customer validation and currency conversion.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Before any remittance, the Taiwan parent must obtain Taiwan-side outbound investment approval, and the WFOE must complete the PRC foreign-invested enterprise registration and FDI foreign-exchange registration with the local SAFE branch through a designated bank. The WFOE then opens an FDI capital settlement account with a Tier-1 domestic bank. The inward wire must arrive via SWIFT MT103 from the parent's own account, with the beneficiary account owned by the WFOE and the remittance purpose clearly stated as FDI equity capital contribution (the SAFE business-code field shown on the FDI registration form). The bank will place the funds in the capital escrow account, perform receipt verification, issue the FDI capital contribution confirmation notice, and, after the supporting documents are validated, permit conversion of the foreign currency into RMB. A licensed CPA then performs statutory capital verification and issues a capital verification report, which is necessary for subsequent changes to registered capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury payments are split into current-account trade/service settlements and capital-account repatriations. For service or trade payments, use SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic transfers with SAFE purpose codes, commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT799) for documentary import/export, and documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for open-account trade; all require underlying contract, invoice, customs declaration or service-trade certificate, and tax withholding proof where applicable. For RMB-denominated outflows, use the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) or cross-border RMB clearing through the settlement bank. Dividend remittances require audited PRC GAAP financial statements, board dividend resolution, tax payment certificate for distributable dividends, and the bank's outbound payment verification; profits cannot exceed audited distributable retained earnings.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/FX forwards are permissible only where the WFOE has a genuine current-account or approved capital-account exposure and the trade is fully documented; no speculative positioning is allowed.
Onshore RMB/FX currency swaps are permissible for hedging the conversion risk of trade settlements, service fees, and short-term working capital flows, subject to SAFE's real-deal-underlying test.

Onshore foreign-exchange options are permissible with a real exposure, with maximum tenors and strike ranges set by the bank's derivatives suitability policy; options must not create leveraged speculative loss.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for the onshore WFOE; the Taiwan parent may execute NDFs offshore to hedge consolidated RMB translation risk, but cannot enter into contracts in the name of the WFOE without SAFE approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting with audited financial statements, operating report, earnings distribution or retained earnings proposal, and subsequent MOEA filing of shareholder-approved statements and minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Office; Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) if the WFOE is classified as a public-issuance company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened on or before 30 June following the fiscal year-end; MOEA filing of the approved statements must be made within 15 days after AGM approval; public-issuance annual financial report filing with FSC is due by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM can trigger a MOEA order calling the meeting; non-filing of approved statements may attract administrative fines of approximately NT$10,000 to NT$50,000; if the company is found to have ceased business for six months or more, MOEA may impose an administrative dissolution order under Taiwan Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (profit-seeking enterprise income tax) including undistributed retained earnings surtax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance, Republic of China
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May immediately following the calendar taxable year; e-filing extension generally permits filing and payment up to 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a surcharge of 2% of the assessed tax for each two-month delinquency period, capped at 20%; false or omitted returns can trigger a deficiency penalty of up to three times the unpaid tax; unpaid amounts accrue late-payment interest and are collectible through lien, garnishment, and forced execution after a 30-day demand notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign investment report covering shareholding, capital flows, dividends, and investment operation data required for the wholly foreign-owned enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after fiscal year-end, i.e., on or before 31 May for a calendar-year WFOE; electronic filing through the MOEAIC portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquent filing subjects the foreign investor or enterprise to administrative fines under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, generally in the NT$30,000 to NT$100,000 range; repeated non-filing may result in suspension of capital repatriation or remittance approvals and, after continued default, administrative dissolution by MOEA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership (UBO) confirmation and registration update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Central Company Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial registration at company incorporation; any change in ultimate beneficial ownership, directors, supervisors, managers, or qualifying shareholders must be filed within 15 days of the relevant change; annual confirmation and ratification must be completed by the AGM date and no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Company Act and anti-money-laundering governing rules, late, incomplete, or inaccurate UBO filing may be penalized in the NT$20,000 to NT$500,000 range per violation; after a rectification order, continued non-compliance can lead to deregistration or administrative strike-off action by the registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Retained earnings surtax return and tax allocation statement for undistributed surplus earnings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance, Republic of China
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due with the annual corporate income tax return on 31 May after fiscal year-end; the 5% retained earnings surtax applies when earnings are retained beyond the statutory prescribed ceiling
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underfiling or loss of retained earnings can trigger a deficiency penalty of up to three times the surtax avoided; late payment interest and enforced collection commence after a 30-day tax demand; sustained failure to file statutory returns may support administrative dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate registration confirmation and corporate records update for directors, supervisors, managers, registered address, and shareholding register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in directors, supervisors, managers, capital, registered office, or controlling shareholding must be filed within 15 days of the corporate act; if there is no change, no separate annual renewal is required, but records must be confirmed as current by the AGM deadline of 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration of material company changes can attract administrative fines of approximately NT$10,000 to NT$50,000; failure to maintain current statutory registers at the registered office is independently penalized; a company that has been inactive for more than six months may be administratively dissolved by MOEA.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 20 and the MOEA enforcement rules, an independent audit by a certified public accountant is compulsory for a non-public cybersecurity SaaS WFOE if any one of the following quantitative thresholds is met: paid-in capital of NT$30 million or more; annual net turnover or sales revenue exceeding NT$50 million; balance-sheet total assets exceeding NT$100 million; or 100 or more full-time employees as prescribed by MOEA guidance. Public-issuance companies, financial institutions, and insurance or securities enterprises are compulsorily audited regardless of size. For companies below these thresholds, no statutory CPA audit is required unless the shareholders resolve to adopt one or an intercompany transaction agreement, lender, or the FSC otherwise mandates a certified audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public-issuance companies must apply IFRS as endorsed by the FSC; non-public WFOEs apply the Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standard (EAS), which is substantially aligned with the IFRS for SMEs framework, or may voluntarily adopt full IFRS. All audited financial statements must be prepared on an accrual basis in New Taiwan Dollars and accompanied by a certified public accountant's opinion in accordance with Taiwan professional auditing standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must maintain a beneficial ownership register and file the mandatory UBO data with the MOEA central company registry. Initial UBO filing is made at incorporation; any transfer of shares or change in a qualifying shareholder, director, supervisor, manager, or ultimate beneficial owner must be reported to MOEA within 15 days of occurrence. An annual confirmation is required to ratify the UBO register as of the annual shareholders' meeting, no later than 30 June; the company secretary or designated manager must certify that the beneficial ownership records are true, complete, and current. Failure to update within the 15-day window is treated as a separate violation and triggers the applicable AML administrative penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges, Mortgages, and Other Security Interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 1,800 per annum for a Taiwan registered office address, registered correspondence agent, and standard annual corporate secretarial retainer
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 12,000 per annum for a non-public cybersecurity SaaS WFOE with a straightforward shareholding structure; USD 8,000 - 20,000 per annum where consolidated financial statements, intercompany transactions, or FSC-regulated reporting obligations are present

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan does not grant a blanket corporate income tax holiday, but qualifying enterprises may use: (i) an R&D investment tax credit for qualifying cybersecurity and software development expenditure; (ii) patent box treatment for qualifying intellectual property derived income, which can effectively reduce the tax rate to 8% on relevant profit; (iii) the free trade zone / offshore income exemption program, where income that is genuinely derived from offshore activities and supported by economic substance may be treated as non-taxable; and (iv) the 10-year net operating loss carryforward permitted by Article 39 of the Income Tax Act, subject to complete accounting records and audited financial statements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form 110), filed through the Ministry of Finance e-Tax electronic filing system for profit-seeking enterprises.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return, with tentative tax prepayment filing in the current year for the first half of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year WFOE, the annual return must be filed between 1 May and 31 May of the year following the tax year. For a special fiscal year, the return is due within five months after the fiscal year-end. The tentative tax prepayment is due each year from 1 September through 30 September, or at the alternative prepayment election using prior-year taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identity and Shareholding Profile
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Unified Business Number, registered address, tax bureau, fiscal year, paid-in capital, and the complete shareholder list including non-resident beneficial owners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan WFOE is a Taiwan resident company and must be declared in the resident corporate taxpayer box, not as a non-resident. The PRC parent and all non-resident shareholders must be disclosed in the shareholder schedule. If the WFOE is controlled by a mainland China parent, the cross-strait relationship must be separately flagged because no comprehensive cross-strait double taxation agreement is currently in force, so no treaty exemption may be claimed based solely on mainland Chinese residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Operating Revenue and Gross Receipts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All Taiwan domestic and cross-border SaaS subscription revenue, cloud vulnerability scanning fees, penetration testing service income, professional service income, maintenance fees, and license fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full worldwide gross revenue of the Taiwan WFOE. Revenue from clients in mainland China, the United States, and the European Union is taxable in Taiwan because the WFOE is a Taiwan tax resident. Do not reduce gross revenue by Stripe processing fees, wire transfer charges, or foreign platform commissions; those are deductible operating expenses but must be evidenced by invoices and foreign payment records. The location of cloud servers alone does not determinatively move revenue outside Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Cost of Goods Sold and Operating Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cloud infrastructure costs, subcontracted cybersecurity services, employee salary costs, rent, software tools, legal and professional fees, insurance, depreciation, and other deductible business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to a related foreign party are scrutinized for economic substance and arm's length pricing. Intercompany royalties, technology license fees, and host service charges paid to the PRC parent or a related regional hub must be supported by a transfer pricing analysis, service evidence, and evidence of the benefit actually received. If the WFOE makes payments to non-residents for royalties or debt interest, the WFOE must withhold income tax at 20% unless a reduced treaty rate is positively substantiated. Payments to non-resident independent contractors are also subject to withholding at the statutory non-resident rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Related-Party Transaction Disclosure and Transfer Pricing Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The complete schedule of cross-border related-party transactions including IP licensing, software resale, management services, cost-sharing arrangements, intercompany loans, and shared cloud infrastructure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The filing must include the mandatory related-party transaction disclosure schedule. A transfer pricing report is required when aggregate related-party transactions reach the statutory threshold, with a lower threshold for service, intangible, and financing transactions. The tested party analysis should recognize the Taiwan WFOE as the party performing valuable cloud security functions, with employees deciding product configuration, client acceptance, threat monitoring, and risk assumption. The tax authority may reject a TP report that treats the Taiwan entity as a mere routine service provider while allocating all residual SaaS profit to the mainland China parent or an offshore holding company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Reconciliation of Accounting Profit to Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of net income per books to taxable income, adding back non-deductible expenses, tax penalties, overseas-related adjustments, and amounts requiring tax-code addbacks.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible intercompany charges, undocumented management fees, excessive royalty payments, and expenses not supported by proper Uniform Invoice or withholding documentation must be added back. Any unaudited accounting loss claimed in the return may be rejected if books and records are incomplete. The WFOE must ensure that the mainland China shareholder does not treat distributions as tax-free return of capital unless there is a documented capital reduction with corporate registration approval and no distribution of accumulated retained earnings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Calculation, Alternative Minimum Tax, Credits, and Foreign Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of regular corporate income tax at 20%, the corporate alternative minimum tax at 12% where applicable, tax credits, prepaid withholding taxes, and the final amount due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE has foreign-source income, a foreign tax credit is allowed only for income sourced outside Taiwan and verified by foreign tax receipts, with the credit capped at the Taiwan tax attributable to that foreign income. The R&D credit and patent box election, if claimed, must be supported by the qualifying expenditure schedule and an economic substance narrative. If the WFOE files a nil tax because of fabricated losses, the tax authority may apply the anti-abuse rules, reject the loss, and impose penalties on both the company and the responsible director.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Declaration, Responsible Person Signature, and Tax Agent Certification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The declaration section signed by the responsible person or director of the WFOE and, if applicable, certified by a licensed tax practitioner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The responsible director is the person accountable for the truthfulness of the return, even if a hired accountant prepares the filing. A non-resident director who participates in the management of Taiwan operations is still treated as a responsible person for tax penalty purposes. Failure to sign or delegation of the filing to an external bookkeeper does not remove the director's personal exposure to civil penalties, departure restrictions, or criminal liability in cases of fraud.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge computed on the unpaid tax for each month or fraction of a month beyond the statutory deadline, plus daily interest on the unpaid balance at the postal savings interest rate. Under Article 108 of the Income Tax Act, failure to file by the prescribed date may lead to an additional administrative penalty of up to 10% of the tax due, subject to minimum fine amounts. Under Article 110, deliberate understatement of taxable income is punishable by an additional penalty of one to three times the evaded tax, and fraudulent evasion is prosecuted under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act, exposing the responsible parties to imprisonment, asset seizure, and travel bans.
